description: Asks the founder to add one of their own domains to the live app. email: true also sends the app's email from mail.<domain> (on a domain already added for the web, that adds email to it). site: true shows the app's Gemmein Live site at it — only when the founder wants their Gemmein site there, never for a domain whose site is hosted elsewhere (on a domain already added, that turns it on). Once done, the answer lists the DNS records for your human to add at their DNS provider — Gemmein never changes anyone's DNS. This is what a founder may call putting it on their own web address. This is a change to how the business runs: your human approves it in their browser with the code Gemmein emails (and, when they set one up, their authenticator app's code). Nothing changes until they approve; approving it carries it out — Gemmein does it the moment they press Approve, once, and records what happened on their Logs. The approval page shows Gemmein's own sentence of the real effect, read against Live; a request that no longer matches Live when it is carried out is refused and nothing changes. Returns the approval link for your human and a handle: live_action_status with wait: true answers the moment it is done, or why not — never ask your human to tell you they approved. A second call asks again (a new approval).
